title: Proactive SLO attestation and backpressure-tuning postmortem
creator: Maya Chen
summary: A multi-region overload event on 2026-02-14 led to an SLO miss for 95th and 99th pct tail latency for customer requests. Root causes included overlapping circuit-breaker windows between region affinity and global fallback, delayed KV cache warmup after cold failover, and an over-aggressive broad-based shed that unintentionally targeted high-priority traffic. This doc captures the timeline, root cause reasoning, mitigations applied during the incident, and longer-term changes we will implement to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-14 11:03 UTC: External traffic surge observed in us-west region after partner release spiked tokenized batch requests.
2026-02-14 11:05 UTC: Per-region latency SLO alarms triggered for us-west; automated cross-region failover began.
2026-02-14 11:06 UTC: Control-plane routed a large percentage of affected keys to eu-west as fallback; regional affinity leases were not fully released.
2026-02-14 11:07 UTC: Circuit breakers in eu-west and us-east entered shedding mode with different hysteresis settings; oscillation between regions observed for ~12 minutes.
2026-02-14 11:09 UTC: KV cache warmup for new region assignments lagged due to cold key misses; per-request latency spiked for long-tail customers.
2026-02-14 11:18 UTC: Runbook executed: temporarily increased short-lived burst capacity and applied conservative global gradient backoff to stabilize routing.
2026-02-14 11:35 UTC: Traffic normalized; SLOs recovered but 95/99 latency metrics showed a persistent bump for the rest of the day for affected customers.
2026-02-14 13:00 UTC: Incident declared mitigated; postmortem initiated.
impact: ~0.7% of total requests experienced >5x latency relative to normal for 95th and 99th pct during the 20-minute window. Several enterprise customers reported degraded interactive experiences. No data loss or model corruption occurred. Billing/usage was unaffected but SLA credits were requested by two large accounts.
root_cause: Misaligned circuit-breaker hysteresis between regions: eu-west used a 30s cooldown, us-west used 90s. When failover redistributed affinity, different cooldowns caused quick re-enablement in one region and immediate re-shedding in another, producing oscillation.

Affinity lease semantics allowed sticky routing despite pipeline-level failover. Leases were long enough that many token groups continued to migrate in small waves rather than a coordinated shift, amplifying cold-cache penalties.
KV cache warmup was reactive instead of predictive: the warmup path only populated on first miss, resulting in a burst of cold misses after mass migration and higher per-request latency.
Single global load-shedding threshold was too coarse. The shed policy used coarse token-count thresholds which inadvertently classified some high-priority interactive traffic as eligible for shed.
Insufficient SLO attestation coverage: the on-call runbook lacked quick diagnostics for cross-region hysteresis mismatch and cache-warmup rates, delaying targeted mitigation.
what_we_did_immediately: Applied an emergency coordinated cooldown override to align circuit-breaker hysteresis across affected regions, preventing further oscillation.
Temporarily extended affinity lease expiry to finish the in-flight migration uniformly and reduce repeated reassignments.
Enabled proactive parallel KV warming for top token prefixes (based on recent access frequency) to reduce cold-miss tail.
Narrowed the shedding classifier to exclude high-priority customer routes and switched to graceful queuing for those routes.
Opened priority support channels with impacted enterprise customers and issued preliminary mitigation transcripts and status updates.
long_term_actions: H1: Implement 'hysteresis convergence' tooling — a control-plane pre-check that ensures circuit-breaker cooldown/hysteresis settings are consistent across candidate failover regions before initiating mass routing changes.
H1: Change affinity lease model to use short adaptive leases with a final forced cutover window; add visibility in console for active lease distribution.
H1: Introduce predictive KV warmup service that uses recent access windows and probabilistic key prefetching to warm new regional caches in parallel ahead of mass migrations.
H1: Replace single global shed threshold with a multi-axis shed decision that includes route priority, observed warmup rate, and token-affinity score.
H2: Add automated SLO attestation checks to the runbook that surface hysteresis divergences, warmup lag, and per-route shed impact within the first 60s of failover.
H2: Build a controlled canary for failover that uses probabilistic (10-20%) early fanout to the fallback region to validate warmup and circuit behavior before full cutover.
H2: Create a post-failover audit in the Console that shows keys migrated, cold-miss curves, and per-region circuit states for forensic review.

metrics_and_signals_to_monitor: Per-region circuit state transitions per minute (goal: <0.5 oscillations/minute post-fix)
Cold-miss rate for top-k prefixes after failover (goal: reduce 99th pct tail by 60%)
Per-route shed invocations and percentage of high-priority traffic affected (goal: zero high-priority sheds).
Time-to-stable after failover (time until 95th pct latency returns to baseline; goal: <90s).
